quizName: DMV Practice Test #16 30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: How can you reduce your reaction time?

options.text: Ride below the speed limit.
Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes.
Shift into neutral when slowing down.
Speed up before turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes.
questions.explanation: When approaching a dangerous area like an intersection, keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes. This reduces the time you need to react to hazards.

questions.question: What should you do when another vehicle is passing you?

options.text: Ride on the left side of your lane.
Ride in the middle of your lane.
Ride on the right side of your lane.
Move onto the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the middle of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the middle of your lane when being passed. Riding on the side nearest the other vehicle increases crash risk. Riding on the far side may cause the other driver to return to your lane too quickly.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black letters or symbols?

options.text: Warning sign
Service sign
Regulatory sign
Speed limit sign

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning sign
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell drivers about upcoming road hazards.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, which instruction should you NOT give them?

options.text: Get on the motorcycle after the engine starts.
Sit as far forward as possible without crowding you.
Hold firmly onto your waist, hips, or belt.
Talk as much as they want.

questions.correctAnswerText: Talk as much as they want.
questions.explanation: Passengers should avoid talking and moving around so you can focus on riding. Passengers should board after the engine starts, sit forward without crowding you, and hold onto your waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: What should you do if road conditions require longer stopping distance?

options.text: Decrease the distance between you and the vehicle ahead.
Increase the distance between you and the vehicle ahead.
Travel on the shoulder.
Have someone else ride your motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase the distance between you and the vehicle ahead.
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance if your motorcycle needs more distance to stop. Use at least a three-second distance when roads are slippery, visibility is poor, or traffic is heavy.

questions.question: What is the best thing to do when it starts raining?

options.text: Speed up.
Exit the road.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
Ride in the center of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: When it rains, the center of the lane becomes slippery. Ride in the tire tracks left by cars instead. The left tire track is often the best choice.

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean?

options.text: Slow or stop
Left turn
Right turn
Backing up

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow or stop
questions.explanation: This hand signal means slow or stop. When a rider's left arm is bent at the elbow and points downward, they are signaling they plan to slow down or stop.

questions.question: How should you brake on a slippery surface?

options.text: Use only the rear brake.
Use only the front brake.
Use both brakes.
Do not brake; downshift instead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes.
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, reduce your speed and avoid sudden movements. Use both brakes together when you need to slow down or stop.

questions.question: What is the best way to stop?

options.text: Squeeze the front brake lever hard.
Keep your knees against the gas tank and look ahead.
Press the rear brake gradually harder.
Use only the front brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your knees against the gas tank and look ahead.
questions.explanation: For the best straight-line braking, apply the brakes smoothly and firmly. As weight moves forward, the front wheel gets more grip, so increase front brake pressure while reducing rear brake pressure. Keep your knees against the gas tank and look ahead to stay in a straight line.

questions.question: For a face shield to work well, it should NOT:

options.text: Have scratches on it.
Block your side vision.
Be airtight.
Come loose easily.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be airtight.
questions.explanation: A good face shield should be scratch-free, let you see to the sides, fasten securely, and allow air to pass through. It should NOT be airtight because that traps moisture and causes fogging, making it hard to see.

questions.question: What is true about the center portion of a lane?

options.text: It is always the best place for a motorcycle to ride.
It often has oil and grease, but it is usually safe to ride on.
It often has oil and grease, and it is never safe to ride on.
It is the smoothest part of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: It often has oil and grease, but it is usually safe to ride on.
questions.explanation: Oil from cars collects in the center of each lane. The road is usually dry enough for motorcycles to ride safely in this area. Avoid areas where oil has built up, like busy intersections or toll booths.

questions.question: When another vehicle passes you on your left, what should you do?

options.text: Move as far to the right as possible to help the other driver.
Move to the shoulder to help the other driver.
Ride in the center of your lane.
Ride on the left side of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center of your lane.
questions.explanation: Stay in the center of your lane when being passed. Riding to the side closest to the passing vehicle risks a collision. Riding to the side farthest away may encourage the driver to return to your lane too soon. The center is the safest position.

questions.question: Which statement about motorcycle brakes is true?

options.text: The front and rear brakes provide equal braking power.
The front brake provides more braking power than the rear brake.
The rear brake provides more braking power than the front brake.
Only the front brake should be used when braking.

questions.correctAnswerText: The front brake provides more braking power than the rear brake.
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful and provides at least 70 percent of the stopping power. Always use both brakes together when you slow down or stop.

questions.question: How should you park a motorcycle next to a curb?

options.text: At a 90-degree angle with the rear wheel touching the curb.
At a 45-degree angle with the front tire touching the curb.
Like a car, with both wheels the same distance from the curb.
At the left edge of the space so drivers can see it better.

questions.correctAnswerText: At a 90-degree angle with the rear wheel touching the curb.
questions.explanation: Park your motorcycle at a 90-degree angle to the curb with your rear wheel touching it.

questions.question: Why should you not move to the far side of your lane when being passed?

options.text: It discourages the passing driver from cutting in too early.
It encourages the passing driver to cut in too early.
It encourages the passing driver to pass quickly.
It encourages other drivers to pass you.

questions.correctAnswerText: It encourages the passing driver to cut in too early.
questions.explanation: Moving to the far side of your lane could encourage the passing driver to return to your lane before it is safe. Stay in the center of your lane when being passed.

questions.question: Why should motorcycle riders not only rely on mirrors?

options.text: Motorcycle mirrors are smaller, so you can't see as much.
Motorcycles have blind spots, just like cars.
Mirrors are never accurate.
Mirrors take your eyes off the road and should not be used.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycles have blind spots, just like cars.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like any other vehicle. You cannot rely only on mirrors to see what is behind you. Check your blind spots frequently by turning your head.

questions.question: Is the oily center strip of a lane safe for motorcycles?

options.text: Never safe.
Usually safe, unless the road is wet.
Usually safe, unless it is sunny.
Always safe, no matter the weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually safe, unless the road is wet.
questions.explanation: Oil collects in the center of traffic lanes. When the road is dry, this area usually has enough grip for safe riding. The oily strip is usually only two feet wide, so you can often ride around one side of it and still stay in the center of the lane.

questions.question: How do you get maximum braking power?

options.text: Use the rear brake only.
Use the front brake only.
Use both brakes.
Use the rear brake while downshifting.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes.
questions.explanation: Use both the front and rear brakes fully to get maximum braking power. Do not lock either wheel. Always use both brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: What should you do to turn on a motorcycle?

options.text: Press the grip in the direction you want to turn.
Press the grip opposite of the direction you want to turn.
Do not hold the grip because it can be dangerous.
Do not lean the motorcycle because it can be unsafe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the grip in the direction you want to turn.
questions.explanation: At speeds faster than walking, your motorcycle must lean to turn. Press the grip in the direction you want to turn. This causes the motorcycle to lean the right way.

questions.question: What happens to face shields and goggles over time?

options.text: They will likely never need to be replaced.
They develop scratches and become brittle, and need regular replacement.
They should be made of breakable materials so they break away in a crash.
They should not allow any air to pass through.

questions.correctAnswerText: They develop scratches and become brittle, and need regular replacement.
questions.explanation: Face shields and goggles are made of plastic. Over time they develop scratches and become brittle. Replace them regularly to stay protected and comfortable.

questions.question: What happens when you brake while turning on a curve?

options.text: Use only the front brake.
It works the same as braking on a straight road.
You will have more traction as you lean into the curve.
You may have less traction as you lean into the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may have less traction as you lean into the curve.
questions.explanation: You can use both brakes while turning, but you must be very careful. When the motorcycle leans into a turn, the tires use some of their grip to make the turn. This means less grip is left for stopping.

questions.question: What does this signal mean?

options.text: Rest stop
High beams on
Turn right
Hazard

questions.correctAnswerText: Hazard
questions.explanation: Signals are an important way riders communicate in groups. When the lead rider extends their right leg, it means there is a hazard on the right side of the road.

questions.question: Without a helmet, a motorcycle rider is ________ more likely to suffer a critical head injury in a crash.

options.text: Three times
Four times
Five times
Six times

questions.correctAnswerText: Five times
questions.explanation: A rider without a helmet is five times more likely to suffer a serious head injury in a crash.

questions.question: When preparing to pass another rider on the left, what should you do?

options.text: Move to the right part of the lane so they can see you in their side mirror.
Move to the left part of the lane to see better ahead.
Stay in the center of the lane so they can see you in their rearview mirror.
Weave in your lane to get their attention.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the left part of the lane to see better ahead.
questions.explanation: Ride in the left part of your lane to see better and to be more visible. Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder for traffic before changing lanes.

questions.question: When exiting a highway as part of a group, which formation should you use?

options.text: Staggered
Single-file
Paired up
Three riders across the lane

questions.correctAnswerText: Single-file
questions.explanation: A staggered formation is best for group riding on straight roads. But switch to single-file when taking curves, turning, or entering or exiting a highway.

questions.question: Proper riding clothing provides all of the following, except:

options.text: Comfort.
Protection in a crash.
Protection from cold weather.
Discomfort.

questions.correctAnswerText: Discomfort.
questions.explanation: Proper clothing helps protect you in a crash. It also protects against weather and other discomforts like wind and cold.

questions.question: To work well, an eye or face shield must:

options.text: Fasten securely.
Block all air flow.
Not allow eyeglasses underneath.
Block your side vision.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fasten securely.
questions.explanation: To work well, an eye or face shield must fasten securely. It should also have no scratches, be hard to penetrate, allow clear side views, let air flow to prevent fogging, and have room for eyeglasses if needed.

questions.question: When preparing to pass a vehicle on the left, why should you ride on the left side of your lane?

options.text: The right side might be slippery.
You can see hazards in the next lane better.
Drivers don't expect to be passed on their left.
It puts you in the car's rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can see hazards in the next lane better.
questions.explanation: Ride in the left part of your lane to see better and be more visible to drivers coming toward you.

questions.question: Most motorcycles have curved, or convex, mirrors. These mirrors:

options.text: Are easy to get used to right away.
Make cars look closer than they really are.
Show a narrow view of the road.
Make cars look farther away than they really are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make cars look farther away than they really are.
questions.explanation: Curved mirrors show a wider view of the road behind you than flat mirrors. However, they make cars look farther away than they actually are. Practice judging distances if you are not used to curved mirrors.

questions.question: When riding, you should:

options.text: Turn your head and shoulders to look through turns.
Keep your arms straight.
Keep your knees away from the gas tank.
Turn only your head and eyes to look through turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn only your head and eyes to look through turns.
questions.explanation: When turning, look ahead to where you want to go. Turn only your head, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level with the horizon.
